sources.entry: ⭐️ karanpratapsingh/system-design: learn how to design systems at scale and prepare for system design interviews

summary.one_liner: A long-form, chapter-based course on system design covering networking, databases, distributed architecture, and case studies, aimed at learning system design and preparing for interviews.
keywords: how to design systems at scale
summary.what_it_does: The README is the table of contents and introductory text of a written system design course, organized into five chapters plus an appendix. Chapter I covers networking and infrastructure basics: IP addressing, the OSI model, TCP vs UDP, DNS, load balancing, clustering, caching, CDNs, proxies, and availability and scalability. Chapter II covers data: SQL and NoSQL databases, replication, indexes, normalization, consistency models, CAP and PACELC, transactions, sharding, and consistent hashing. Chapter III covers architecture patterns such as N-tier, message brokers and queues, pub-sub, monoliths vs microservices, event sourcing, CQRS, API gateways, and REST/GraphQL/gRPC. Chapter IV covers reliability and security topics such as rate limiting, circuit breakers, idempotency, service discovery, SLAs, disaster recovery, OAuth/OIDC, SSO, and TLS. Chapter V covers interview preparation and worked designs for a URL shortener, WhatsApp, Twitter, Netflix, and Uber. The sections shown in the README are explanatory prose with comparison tables and lists of example products.
use_cases: understanding DNS, TCP/UDP, and load balancing
choosing consistency models like CAP or ACID vs BASE
studying microservices and event-driven architecture patterns
reviewing worked designs for large consumer apps
notable: Organized as a sequential course with five chapters covering networking, data, architecture, reliability, and case studies
Includes a worked TCP vs UDP comparison table and a step-by-step DNS lookup walkthrough
Chapter V includes interview-style designs for URL shortener, WhatsApp, Twitter, Netflix, and Uber
Also available as a website version and an ebook on Leanpub, according to the README
caveats: Content is conceptual and explanatory; it does not contain runnable code or a software project
Many sections are high-level overviews, and the README does not describe depth of each case study in the visible portion
The README is truncated in the provided text, so later chapters were not fully visible
